data.name: The Thrill of the Fight - VR Boxing
data.detailed_description:
The Thrill of the Fight is a down-to-earth VR boxing game focused on authenticity. Enter a virtual gym and battle a series of unique challengers with their own styles and techniques. Use timing and skill to land the knockout blow. Evade swings, land jabs, and block punches to become the king of the ring!

Room scale is required with a minimum supported play area size of 2m by 2m (6.5ft by 6.5ft). Please ensure your SteamVR Chaperone boundaries or Oculus Guardian boundaries are set up properly for room scale and that you are willing to move and punch anywhere within and around the play area you have defined. Joystick movement is not supported, and you are expected to physically move around in the real-world.

Oculus Quest is not supported. Do not purchase the PC version of The Thrill of the Fight to play using the Quest headset. Oculus Link does not fully implement all of the room scale features that The Thrill of the Fight relies on to work properly. The only functional and supported way to play The Thrill of the Fight on Quest is to play the native Quest version.

data.short_description: The Thrill of the Fight is a room-scale only VR boxing game focused on authenticity. Face off in the virtual ring where you'll jab, dodge, and sweat your way to the top of the boxing world. Grab your gloves, step through the ropes, and become a champion.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows 7 SP1 or newer
  • Processador: Intel Core i5-4590/AMD Ryzen 5 1600 equivalent or better
  • Memória: 8 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 970, AMD Radeon R9 290 equivalent or better
  • DirectX: Versão 11
  • Compatibilidade com R.V.: SteamVR or Oculus Rift (Oculus Quest not supported). Requires motion controllers. Room Scale 2m by 2m (6.5ft by 6.5ft) area required. Joystick movement not supported.

reviews.review:
I've had this game for a while now and played it plenty, however a recent update, seemingly targeted at the Steam Frame release, messed with my controller alignment and made it look like I have two left hands, initially I tried rolling back to previous versions but they each have quirks that make that unappealing, so I tried just tolerating having a hand that looks weird but is mostly usable for punching.
It was then I discovered other changes I hadn't noticed, firstly some graphical updates which I don't really care either way about, but more importantly the physics of punching now feels different, my run through of the various boxers was now noticeably easier and more 'samey', and certain settings I remember seeing are now like wrist alignment are gone from the menu. It's possible that tracking my particular controllers has actually gotten better and that's manifested as less difficulty, but considering I still have two left hands I don't think that's what's going on.
If the game worked as it used to, I would have almost no problems with it, but the fact it currently doesn't work and I have effectively had the game changed around under my feet means I can't really recommend it, especially when the game sat dormant for years completely fine and only got these changes because of a headset release and not for any other reason.
